Let’s talk about Billy Joel

Who is Billy Joel?

Billy Joel (b. 1949) is an American singer and pianist. He is one of the best-selling singers in history, having released pop, rock and classical music. Over his 50+ year, Billy Joel has won five Grammys, has received Kennedy Center Honors (the highest honor for contribution to American arts) and has received the Gershwin Prize for Popular Song. He is widely considered one of the most influential American singers of all time.

His quote:

“Musicians want to be the loud voice for so many quiet hearts.”

- Billy Joel (1993 Berklee College of Music Commencement Speech)

His albums:

  • Cold Spring Harbor (1971)

  • Piano Man (1973)

  • Streetlife Serenade (1974)

  • Turnstiles (1976)

  • The Stranger (1977)

  • 52nd Street (1978)

  • Glass Houses (1980)

  • The Nylon Curtain (1982)

  • An Innocent Man (1983)

  • The Bridge (1986)

  • Storm Front (1989)

  • River of Dreams (1993)

  • Fantasies and Delusions (2001)

Data Analysis:

Import Data:

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)

df <- read.csv("singers_2023/Billy_Joel.csv")

Data Frame:

df |> dplyr::slice_sample(n=5) |> knitr::kable(digits=2)
artist_name track_name track_number album_name album_release_year energy valence danceability loudness speechiness liveness tempo key_mode duration_ms

Billy Joel Odoya 1 A Matter of Trust - The Bridge to Russia: The Music (Live) 2014 0.34 0.17 0.35 -14.09 0.04 0.06 117.00 A# minor 76040

Data Preparation:

I’ve removed tracks that were duplicated to clean the data. I have also removed live versions of tracks and removed the classical albums to keep the dataset consistent.

#removing duplicates
df = df |> distinct(track_name, .keep_all = TRUE)
#removing live and piano songs
df = df |> filter(!grepl("Live|Opus", album_name))
#numeric to character
df$album_name = as.character(df$album_name)

Album Analysis (Valence and Energy):

#boxplot
ggplot(df, aes(x=as.factor(album_release_year), y=valence)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x="Album Name", y="Valence")

We can see that Billy Joel’s albums there is no clear trend in terms of valence. We can notice that the album released in 1982 (The Nylon Curtain) has a very low median and does not follow the generally high valence trend of Billy’s Joel’s later career years. It turns out Billy Joel got divorced in 1982, which explains the very sad album!

Maybe the spread of energy will tell us more?

ggplot(df, aes(x=as.factor(album_release_year), y=energy))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  labs(x="Album name", y="Energy")

We can see that Billy Joel’s albums have tended to get more energetic as time has passed. Billy Joel’s first album (Cold Spring Harbor, 1971) is particularly notable for its low energy. This may be because there were technical problems in the mastering of the album, causing the album to be a critical and commercial failure. Maybe Billy Joel learned from this and made his albums more energetic to gain more success?

subgroup <-df|> filter(track_name%in% c("Piano Man", "Uptown Girl", "Vienna"))

ggplot(df, aes(x = valence, y = energy, color = album_name))+
  geom_point()+ 
  geom_hline(yintercept= 0.5, color="grey")+ 
  geom_vline(xintercept= 0.5, color="grey")+ 
  geom_text(data=subgroup, aes(label=track_name))

We can see that Billy Joel’s music tends to be either Happy or Sad, with very little Angry or Calm music. His most successful song extremely Happy and energetic, which may have pushed him to continue putting out happy and energetic music.

3 Most Positive Songs:

df |> slice_max(valence, n=3) |> dplyr::select(track_name, album_name, album_release_year, valence) |> knitr::kable(digits = 2)

3 Least Energetic Songs:

df |> slice_min(energy, n=3) |> dplyr::select(track_name, album_name, album_release_year, energy) |> knitr::kable(digits = 2)
track_name album_name album_release_year energy
Nocturne Cold Spring Harbor 1971 0.04
Souvenir Streetlife Serenade 1974 0.06
And So It Goes Storm Front 1989 0.09

By analyzing the most/least positive (valence) and most/least energetic songs, we can see that this trend has generally continued, with many of the most positive and most energetic songs being released after 1980.
